key_insight: KAISEN is a five-phase, reproducible auditing pipeline that stress-tests subgroup fairness checks for clinical risk models and shows that some audit components are reliable while others can fail silently under realistic conditions.
engineering_relevance: For ML systems in healthcare, the work shows that fairness audits must report subgroup-specific uncertainty, sensitivity to thresholds, and cohort drift rather than relying on a single aggregate disparity number.
method: Synthetic benchmark across 16 disease tasks, 15 Healthy People 2030 social-determinant axes, and three intersectional subgroups
Five audit phases: subgroup stratification, disparity measurement, mechanism diagnostics, post-hoc mitigation, and drift monitoring
Stress-tested each component to failure with controlled ground truth and released reproducible code/artifacts
evidence_signal: Evaluation on synthetic data with known ground truth found strong disparity-detection trends across axes, 48/48 EOD improvements from per-group threshold tuning, but zero recovery of 48 model-driven mechanism cases under proxy misspecification and cohort-dependent CUSUM failures.
watch_item: The benchmark is synthetic, so the reported audit behavior and fairness conclusions do not establish clinical validity or guarantee transfer to real patient cohorts.
paper_title: KAISEN: Reproducible Subgroup Fairness Auditing for Clinical Risk Models
